meaning: It's okay / I'm fine — but the emotional temperature depends entirely on tone and context.
nuance: Can mean genuine reassurance, a polite deflection, or a quiet 'I'm not okay but don't push it.' Listen to the pause before it.
example_en: Are you really okay? ...Yeah, I'm fine.

meaning: Jackpot / no way! / that's amazing — an all-purpose exclamation of surprise.
nuance: Used for both great news and shocking news. Tone and face tell you which.

meaning: Gaslighting — psychological manipulation where someone deliberately distorts facts so the other person doubts their own memory or judgment.
nuance: Korean adoption of the English term; used the same way as in English pop-psychology discourse.

meaning: To criticize or hate on something unfairly, for reasons that don't really hold up.
Cute! — the digits "700" visually resemble ㄱㅇㅇ, the initial consonants of 귀여워 ("cute"), so it's typed as a quick reaction to something adorable.
nuance: Part of a family of consonant/number code-slang; the reverse "0700" is used to mean "not cute."

meaning: "Actually, this is better" — spinning a setback into a silver lining, sincerely or ironically.
nuance: Popularized around 2018 from internet broadcast (BJ) culture. Note: the source PDF's OCR rendered this headword as "52려좋아" — verified online as 오히려좋아.

meaning: Shorthand for "just handle it well, cleanly, and with good sense" — trusting someone to get something right without detailed instructions.
"What matters is a heart that doesn't break" — shorthand for staying resilient no matter the outcome.
nuance: Popularized from esports commentary as a mantra for not giving up after a loss.

meaning: "Wait, why is this actually true?!" — reacting to a surprising twist that turns out to be real.
"Stomach dress-up" — slang for eating (dressing up your stomach with food).
"Brain dress-up" — slang for studying (dressing up your brain).
Someone hiding real strength or skill behind an unassuming appearance — looks ordinary, is secretly impressive.
Short for "reality-check time" — the sudden moment you're forced to face an uncomfortable truth about your situation.
Short for "trending video" (인기 급상승 동영상) — a video blowing up on YouTube.
Punning on a hot dog brand name to mean "so sleep-deprived you're exhausted" — from 통 못 자 ("couldn't sleep a wink"), which sounds like 통모짜.
"Let's live comfortably in this complicated world" — a laid-back life motto.
"Who even are you [to say that]?" — a sharp pushback when someone acts self-important.
Short for "sunbae-nim" (respected senior) — often tacked onto a crush's name.
"Forced tension" — the fake-cheerful reaction you put on in an awkward group or situation.
Shorthand for "strict, stern, and serious" — describing an overly no-nonsense mood or person.
"My bias is my bias, and [actor] Cha Eun-woo is Cha Eun-woo" — admitting someone else is objectively good-looking without betraying your own favorite.
"Plant butler" — someone who keeps and cares for houseplants.
Someone who acts as frustratingly slow or unclear as if they'd eaten too much sweet potato (고구마) — the opposite of a quick, satisfying reaction.
"Immunity pass from criticism" — earned after doing something impressive enough that people stop calling you out.
A dismissive "so what, go watch TV" — a mock-childish comeback to a complaint.
Short for "a clash of two proud geniuses" — used for a matchup between two evenly matched, highly confident rivals.
A café with "good vibes" — a pun blending 분위기 좋은 (good atmosphere) and 카페 (café).
An expression evoking the sound of savoring or drooling over delicious food.
nuance: Popularized by the mukbang YouTuber '상윤쓰' as a catchphrase.

meaning: Short for "awkward relationship" (어색한 사이).
"Kangaroo tribe" — young adults who are old enough (or even employed) but still financially dependent on their parents.
Short for "chicken for dinner tonight?" — a casual invite to order fried chicken.
"Turn around, cook rice, turn around, cook rice" — the endless cycle of meal-prepping for a household.
Work-life balance.
Short for "were you curious, or did you actually ask?" — calling out someone for asking an unnecessary question.
"Your form/skill is insane" — usually a compliment on someone's performance, occasionally used sarcastically.
"Dragging up every last bit of your soul" — scraping together every possible source of money, often for a big investment like real estate or stocks.
Short for "honestly speaking" (솔직히 까놓고 말해서).
"Stagnant water" — someone who's played the same game for so long they're a veteran fixture of it.
Short for "insider" — someone actively involved and well-liked within their social group.
Shorthand YouTubers use asking viewers for "likes, comments, subscribe, and notifications on."
"Crispy outside, moist inside" — the ideal texture for fried or baked food.
"Case by case" — it depends on the situation.
"I'd rather freeze to death than give up iced coffee" — someone who drinks iced coffee even in freezing winter.
"Completely my style" — something that's exactly your taste.
Short for "emotional wound" (마음의 상처).
Studying at a café.
"Lip-smacking PhD" — someone who really knows their food.
"A disaster you brought on yourself" — self-inflicted trouble.
"I have plenty to say, but I won't" — biting your tongue instead of arguing back.
Gyeongsang-dialect meme for "what's going on?" (무슨 일이고).
"Didn't ask, don't care" — a blunt dismissal of unsolicited information.
"Too Much Information" — used when someone shares more detail than anyone wanted to know.
"Mask scammer" — someone who looks much more attractive with a mask on than without one.
Short for "portable battery" (보조 배터리) — a pun on the standard word 보배 ("treasure").
"A successful fan" — someone whose obsessive fandom (덕후) actually pays off, e.g. meeting or working with their idol.
Short for "nice to meet you, please treat me well" (만나서 반가워, 잘 부탁해).
"Today's workout: complete" — a fitness-culture hashtag.
"If I do it, it's romance; if someone else does it, it's an affair" — calling out a double standard.
A pun on "small but certain happiness" (소확행) — "small but certain embezzlement," joking about skimming a little extra for yourself.
Describes doing something bit by bit — gathering a very small amount at a time.
nuance: Could not independently confirm this term/definition online — lowest-confidence entry in this batch, flagged for extra scrutiny.

meaning: "Sunfish" — a person who's easily startled or mentally fragile, referencing the (exaggerated) idea that ocean sunfish die from minor stress.
Short for "KakaoTalk profile picture."
"Are you the carrot?" — the greeting strangers use to identify each other for a Danggeun Market (당근마켓) resale meetup.
Short for "the title is the content" (제목이 곧 내용) — a post where the title says it all.
Short for "dinner menu recommendation" (저녁 메뉴 추천).
Short for "already-selected seat" — the frustrating message when a concert/ticket seat you wanted is already taken.
"Watch a broadcast as just a broadcast" — a reminder not to take a streamer or TV persona's on-air behavior as who they really are.
A playful pun using the word for "fish" to mean "birthday present" (생일 선물).
A pun where the bank name "NongHyup Bank," said with an accent, sounds like "so pretty" (너무 예쁘네요) — now used as a compliment.
nuance: Origin story: a non-native Korean speaker's mispronunciation was misheard as a compliment, and it stuck as a meme.

meaning: Short for "unsubscribe" (구독 취소).
Short, often sarcastic, for "can you even function in daily life?" (일상생활 가능?).
Short for "pursuing a natural (non-arranged) meeting" — preferring to meet a partner organically rather than through setups or apps.
"Suddenly the mood turns cold" — when a joke or comment kills the room's vibe.
An exaggerated "royally annoyed" — using "King" as an intensifier for irritation.
"The comments are a total mess" — a comment section that's descended into chaos.
"Person by person" — it varies depending on who you ask.
"Looks done-up, but not done-up" — an effortless-looking style that actually took effort.
Short for "ask me anything" (무엇이든 물어보세요).
Blocking a path or road.
To be parched — your throat or mouth feels dry as if burning.
nuance: Unlike most entries in this batch, this is a standard dictionary word (조갈/燥渴), not internet-coined slang — included as-is since it was part of the source list.

meaning: A stylized misspelling of "명언" (famous/wise quote), popular in meme captions.
Short for "please give this a lot of attention" (많은 관심 부탁드립니다).
"Abbreviating even the most random things" — poking fun at how much modern slang shortens phrases.
Short for "lunch menu recommendation" (점심 메뉴 추천).
